turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): In you come. Doctor's ready for you now.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks for hanging on. What has you in?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): It's nothing, really. A bit of an itch on the hands. I nearly didn't come.
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Don't mind him. He's been clawing his fingers and his waist half the night, and we're all in the one house.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Where exactly is it itchy?
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): Between the fingers, and a small bit at the waistband. Only a nuisance.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): When is it worst?
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): Night time, I'd say. In the day I'm grand.
[SEG0009] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The little fella scratches his tummy in the bed too, and my wrists are at me as well.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long has it been going on?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Two days. A couple of days, maybe. Nothing at all.
[SEG0012] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Two days my eye. It's three weeks, since before the Easter break at school.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): We won't pin the start today. Let me look at the hands and the waist.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. There are little tracks between the fingers, and a few raised bumps along the waist. It doesn't look infected.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever with it?
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): No. No fever. Not a bit sick.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any cough?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): No cough.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your weight, have you lost any?
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Umm. Maybe a pound, maybe I haven't. No scales in the house. I'm grand.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): How's the tummy? Any upset?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): No, stomach's fine. Eating away.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): What medicines are you on, so I know what we're working around?

[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): Amlodopine, five milligrams, in the morning for the pressure. The cholesterol one at night, twenty milligrams. Sugar tablets, two of them with the breakfast, err, I forget the name of them. And only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning, from the health shop.

[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): That helps. With the night-time itch, the webs of the fingers, and the whole house scratching, I'd say this is scabies. I wouldn't fully rule out eczema, but I won't park it as eczema and leave it. We don't need blood tests for this.

[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll use permethrin cream, five percent. Spread it from the neck down to the toes, in between the fingers, under the nails, over the waist and the soles. Leave it eight to twelve hours, wash it off, and do the same again in seven days.

[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): The same night, everyone in the house gets it, you and your partner and the child, even if you think the itch is small. Hot wash the sheets, towels and clothes at 60 degrees, and bag whatever won't wash for three days.
[SEG0028] person_1 (NURSE): I'll print those steps out for ye before you go, so you've them in the hand.
[SEG0029] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll make sure he actually uses the cream. He'd skip it.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll see you back in a fortnight and we'll have another look at the skin.
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): Right so. Seems a lot of fuss, but grand.

spec.situation: Itchy rash between fingers and at the waist, worse at night, partner and child also itch; permethrin cream explained step by step; household treatment and washing advice.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

bad.reason: Itch, sites, night worsening, duration disagreement supported; 'rash' and certainty from patient not directly stated by patient.
bad.text: Itchy rash (category=dermatological, status=present, duration=approximately 2 days to 3 weeks, temporality=current, body_site=between the fingers and waist, aggravating_factors=night, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Negative finding asked and answered: patient denied feeling sick ('No fever. No fever. Not a bit sick.').
Negative finding asked and answered: no clear weight loss; patient said 'Maybe a pound, maybe I haven't. No scales in the house,' indicating weight loss was uncertain rather than present.
Past medical history implied by current medicines: high cholesterol/dyslipidaemia (on a nightly 20 mg cholesterol tablet).
Past medical history implied by current medicines: diabetes (on 'sugar tablets', two with breakfast).
Household contact symptoms not captured: family member reported the child scratches his tummy in bed and the family member's wrists are itchy as well.
Assessment/plan detail: doctor stated blood tests are not needed for this presentation.
Treatment plan detail recorded incompletely: everyone in the house should be treated the same night, including the partner as well as the child, even if symptoms are minimal.
